newsitem.title: USA: US investment agency plans boost support in Russia.
newsitem.headline: US investment agency plans boost support in Russia.

text.p: The Overseas Private Investment Corp, an independent agency that provides support for U.S. investments abroad, hopes to expand its programs in Russia, the head of the agency said Thursday.
OPIC President Ruth Harkin, who spoke with reporters following a trip to Russia, said the agency's programs met with success last year, making her optimistic for the future.
However, she said much would depend on legislative changes that would improve the climate for businesses in Russia.

"The investments that we're supporting are really the tip of the iceberg," Harkin said. "If, in fact, various changes are made on a number of points within the Russian legislature on regulatory reform, we'll be able to do a lot more."
Among issues she said needed to be addressed were the tax structure, transparency of state-owned agencies and crime.
OPIC, which sells "political risk" insurance to companies, extended around $1 billion in support to 40 U.S. investments last year.
Harkin said she met various Russian officials during her trip, including Presidential Chief of Staff Anatoly Chubais.
She said that Chubais expressed confidence about the prospects for regulatory reform.
